questions.q: Why does a native roll-up summary field require a master-detail relationship instead of a lookup?
options: Master-detail guarantees the child can't be orphaned, which is what the stored aggregate depends on
Lookup relationships don't support numeric fields
Roll-up summary fields are only available on standard objects
Master-detail relationships are always many-to-many
questions.explain: A lookup relationship allows a child to exist without a parent, which would break a stored aggregate. Master-detail enforces that every child belongs to exactly one parent.

A custom object with two master-detail relationships, one to each side of a many-to-many relationship
A field that joins text from two other fields
A sandbox used to merge two production orgs
questions.explain: A junction object sits between two objects with a master-detail relationship to each, which is the standard declarative way to model many-to-many relationships.

questions.q: What out-of-the-box object does Salesforce ship specifically as a junction between Opportunities and Contacts?
options: OpportunityLineItem
AccountContactRelation
OpportunityContactRole
CampaignMember
questions.explain: OpportunityContactRole is Salesforce's standard junction object linking Opportunities and Contacts many-to-many.

questions.q: A Course object needs a count of enrolled students, and each Student needs a count of enrolled courses, from the same Enrollment junction object. How is this achieved natively?
options: One roll-up summary field shared by both objects
A single master-detail relationship pointing both directions
Two separate roll-up summary fields — one on Course counting Enrollment, one on Student counting Enrollment — each using its own master-detail relationship
This requires Apex; it cannot be done declaratively
questions.explain: Because the junction object has two independent master-detail relationships, each parent object (Course and Student) gets its own roll-up summary field counting the same junction records from its own side.

questions.q: A Project object wants a roll-up of values from a Task object two relationship levels below it (Project -> Phase -> Task). What's the core limitation at play?
options: Roll-up summary fields can only count, never sum
A native roll-up summary field only reaches its direct children, one level down — it can't jump straight from a grandparent to a grandchild
Roll-up summary fields can't be filtered
Only standard objects support roll-up summaries
questions.explain: Native roll-ups are strictly one level. Reaching a grandchild requires a second roll-up at the intermediate level, a Flow, or a tool like DLRS.
